extracted.intended_audience: librarians, children's authors and illustrators, publishers, and CILIP members involved in nominations and judging
extracted.subtask_description: Official Awards Process and eligibility/mission criteria for the CILIP Carnegie Medals, describing what books may be nominated, how nominations and judging proceed, and the values the Medals seek to reward (writing or illustration that creates outstanding reading experiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core award standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Carnegie Medals are awarded annually to books for children and young people that create outstanding reading experiences through writing or illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions (longlists, shortlists, winners) are made by the judging panel of librarians based on the official Medals' criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official separate criteria for writing and illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: There are distinct 'Medal for Writing Criteria' and 'Medal for Illustration Criteria' (linked from the Awards pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges use the official Medals' criteria (writing or illustration) when deciding longlists, shortlists and winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — celebrate outstanding writing and illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards mission includes: 'Celebrating outstanding writing and illustration for children and young people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a core evaluative aim guiding nominations and judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — recognise broad perspectives, experiences and voices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards aim to 'Recognis[e] a broad range of perspectives, experiences and voices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection should reflect and value a diversity of viewpoints in children's books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — champion librarians' role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards mission includes 'Championing the power of librarians to connect children and young people with outstanding books that represent their identities and help them shape a better world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is uniquely nominated and judged by librarians, reflecting this emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — encourage creation of diverse books
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards aim to 'Encourag[e] authors, illustrators and publishers to create more books for children and young people that reflect all identities and promote diversity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and creators are expected to consider representation and identity in submissions and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — promote a readership and market valuing diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards aim to 'Promot[e] a readership and market that values diversity, representation and inclusion in books for children and young people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is intended to influence market and readership preferences toward inclusive books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — challenge children with diverse ideas to promote empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards aim to 'Challeng[e] children and young people with a diversity of ideas and perspectives to promote empathy and understanding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that broaden perspective and foster empathy are within the Awards' evaluative remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — publication date and territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles must have been first published in the UK or Ireland between 1 September and 31 August of the previous calendar year. Books first published in another country must have been co-published in the UK or Ireland within three months of the original publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is strictly applied during eligibility checks before the nominations list is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — language and intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be written in the English language (either as an original work in English or a first English translation of a foreign-language work) and specifically published for children and young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only first English translations are eligible; the work must be targeted at the children/young people market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — co-authorship and anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The book may be co-authored; however, multiple author anthologies are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single co-authored works are acceptable, but collections with multiple authors (anthologies) are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — e-books and previously-published pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of e-books and short stories or poetry previously published in a magazine or elsewhere, the point of publication should be considered as the date when the work is published as a whole. At least 75% of the complete work must be original material published for the first time within the specified time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing eligibility, judges/administrators should treat the 'whole' publication date as the relevant date and verify the 75% original-material threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — formats and categories included
rubrics_metrics.description: All categories of books, including poetry, non-fiction and graphic novels, in print or ebook format, for children and young people are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Awards accept a broad range of formats and genres within children's publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — previous winners allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Books by previous Carnegie and/or Kate Greenaway Medal winners are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior award status of the author/illustrator does not disqualify a new title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process — who may nominate and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations open in September each year and members of CILIP are able to nominate one title per Medal and explain how that title meets the Medals criteria. In addition, several external nominations bodies that share CILIP’s values and mission for the Awards are invited to nominate one title per Medal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators must supply an explanation of how the title meets the Medals' criteria; nomination is limited to one title per Medal per nominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility verification before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Every book that receives a nomination is checked and verified for eligibility before the Nominations list is published in November each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative eligibility checks occur before publicising the nominations list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: All books nominated are read and considered by the librarians that form the panel of judges. The judging panel meet to decide the longlists, then the shortlists and finally, the Medal winners, based on the official Medals’ criteria. Longlists are published in February and shortlists in March, with the winners announced at a ceremony in June.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is librarian-led and follows a staged public timetable (longlist → shortlist → winner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers' contribution for shortlisted titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers of titles that are shortlisted for either of the Medals will be asked to contribute a sum of approx. £2.5k per shortlisted title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fee is used to help fund the design, print and distribution of shortlist publicity materials into approx. 2500 UK schools and public libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shadowers' Choice Awards — selection and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Shadowing groups are invited to vote for their favourite book from each shortlist when voting opens in June; the Shadowers’ Choice Awards are voted for and presented by shadowers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners of the Shadowers’ Choice Award are presented with a medal at the winners’ ceremony; this is a separate, shadower-voted recognition distinct from the main Medals.
